item.title: “Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them,…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then delight ceases. Migajāla, I say that with the cessation of delight, suffering ceases. Sounds … Odors … Tastes … Touches … Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then delight ceases. Migajāla, I say that with the cessation of delight, suffering ceases.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.64
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: The Blessed One replied to Upasīva: “Mindful, not longing for anything, You will cross the flood. Abandoning sensual desires, free from doubt, Day and night…
item.description:
The Blessed One replied to Upasīva:
“Mindful, not longing for anything,
You will cross the flood.
Abandoning sensual desires, free from doubt,
Day and night see clearly —
The destruction of craving is Nibbāna.”

“One who is completely dispassionate
Toward all sensual pleasures,
Depending on nothing, giving up all else —
Freed completely, that is the supreme liberation.
There, that one abides,
And does not go on.”

“Just as a flame blown by strong wind
Goes to its end and cannot be measured,
So too the sage, freed from name and body,
Goes to his end and cannot be measured.”

“For one who has reached the end,
There is no measure by which one could speak of him.
When all phenomena are uprooted,
All paths of speech are uprooted as well.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 5.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: The inner fetter and the outer fetter — Beings are entangled in these fetters. I ask Gotama about this — Who can escape these fetters?…
item.description:
The inner fetter and the outer fetter —
Beings are entangled in these fetters.
I ask Gotama about this —
Who can escape these fetters?

(The Blessed One)
A person established in virtue, wise,
Developing mind and wisdom,
Ardent and discreet —
That monk can escape the fetters.
One who has abandoned greed,
Hatred, and ignorance,
The defilement-free arahant —
He has escaped the fetters.
Where name-and-form is destroyed
Without remainder,
Where the hindrance and perceptions of form are destroyed —
There the fetters are cut.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 7.6
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple reflects: ‘Sensual pleasures present and future, perceptions of sensual pleasure present and future, forms present and future, perceptions of forms…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple reflects: ‘Sensual pleasures present and future, perceptions of sensual pleasure present and future, forms present and future, perceptions of forms present and future — both are impermanent. What is impermanent is not fit to delight in, not fit to welcome, not fit to cling to.’ While he practices thus, dwells often thus, his mind becomes serene in that element. With serene mind, he attains the Imperturbable either in this very life or he becomes strongly inclined to wisdom. At the breakup of the body, after death, it is possible that his consciousness, proceeding accordingly, may attain the Imperturbable.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 106 – Āneñjasappāyasutta

item.title: Elder Bhalliya: “Who drives away the army of Death, As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds — Victorious, fearless, Having subdued,…
item.description:
Elder Bhalliya:
“Who drives away the army of Death,
As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds —
Victorious, fearless,
Having subdued, he dwells at peace.”

From: Theragāthā 1.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nun Abhayā: O fearless nun! This body is so fragile — Worldlings here, Delighting, are often lustful. I will abandon this body, Mindful and…
item.description:
Elder Nun Abhayā:

O fearless nun!
This body is so fragile —
Worldlings here,
Delighting, are often lustful.
I will abandon this body,
Mindful and clearly comprehending.

Without heedlessness, I will strive,
I will strive to escape the painful state.
With craving destroyed, I have attained —
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

From: Therīgāthā 2.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I…
item.description:
“One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I understand, Well-gone One!” - “How, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?” - “One who clings to form, venerable sir, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One’s brief statement thus.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! Thus you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.63

item.title: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is an arahant.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights…
item.description:
“Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in the eye does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.19
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and…
item.description:
“Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: ‘Good man, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may meet death or deadly suffering.’ That man might eat it without reflection, without refusal. While eating, he does not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he meets death or deadly suffering. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has painful results in the future.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 46 – Mahādhammasamādānasutta
📖 Read this sutta
